description: Fly.io deployment config for Open Notebook (self-hosted NotebookLM alternative) — two apps, ~$5/mo with auto-stop
readmeMarkdown:
# Open Notebook on Fly.io

Fly.io deployment config for [Open Notebook](https://github.com/lfnovo/open-notebook),
a self-hosted, privacy-first NotebookLM alternative.

Upstream ships a `docker-compose.yml` and documents Docker, single-container and
from-source installs, but has no cloud deployment guide. This maps its two services onto
**two Fly apps** in one org, connected over Fly's private network:

| Fly app | image | exposure |
|---|---|---|
| `open-notebook-db` | `surrealdb/surrealdb:v2` | private (`.flycast`), always-on |
| `open-notebook-af` | `lfnovo/open_notebook:v1-latest` | **public** HTTPS, auto-suspend |

Traffic: browser → **open-notebook-af** `:8502` (Next.js) → internal rewrite → `:5055` (FastAPI)
→ **open-notebook-db** (`.flycast:8000`). Only the app has a public IP.

The app image runs supervisord with three processes in one container — API, frontend, and
the background worker that handles source processing, embeddings and podcast generation.

## ⚠️ Choose your own app names first

**Fly.io app names are globally unique** (shared across all Fly users), so the example names
below — `open-notebook`, `open-notebook-db` — are almost certainly already taken. Pick your
own (e.g. add a personal suffix: `open-notebook-xyz`).

Your instance is reachable at `https://<app-name>.fly.dev`, which is public and the name is
guessable, so pick something non-obvious **and** set `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` (below).

If you change a name, update it in **every** place it appears:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| app name | `app/fly.toml` → `app` |
| db app name | `db/fly.toml` → `app` |
| public URL | `app/fly.toml` → `API_URL` **and** `CORS_ORIGINS` (`https://<app>.fly.dev`) |
| db hostname | `app/fly.toml` → `SURREAL_URL` (`ws://<db-app>.flycast:8000/rpc`) |

Rename all at once (run in repo root, swap in your names):
```bash
sed -i 's/open-notebook-db/YOUR-db/g; s/open-notebook/YOUR-app/g' app/fly.toml db/fly.toml README.md
```
(Run the `-db` substitution first — it's the longer string, so this order is required.)
Then use the same names in the `fly` commands below.

## Prerequisites
- [`fly` CLI](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/) installed and `fly auth login` done
- `openssl` (for generating secrets)

## Two setups: auto-stop or always-on

`app/fly.toml` ships configured for **auto-stop**. Switching to **always-on** is a two-line
edit in the `[http_service]` block — there is no other difference, and the block is commented
with both sets of values.

| | auto-stop (default) | always-on |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_stop_machines` | `'suspend'` | `'off'` |
| `min_machines_running` | `0` | `1` |
| Cost | **~$5/mo** | **~$16/mo** |
| First request after idle | ~1-3s resume | instant |
| Long background jobs | torn down on suspend — see gotchas | always finish |

Pick auto-stop if you use it interactively and don't mind babysitting podcast generation.
Pick always-on if you want to fire off long jobs and walk away.

### Cost breakdown (rough, LA region)

```
                          auto-stop      always-on
db 512mb always-on        ≈ $3.32/mo     ≈ $3.32/mo
volumes (1GB + 3GB)       ≈ $0.60/mo     ≈ $0.60/mo
app machine               ≈ $1/mo        ≈ $11.83/mo
                          ──────────     ───────────
                            ~$5/mo         ~$16/mo
```

Reference prices: shared-cpu-1x 256mb $2.02, 512mb $3.32; shared-cpu-2x 2gb $11.83,
4gb $22.22; volumes $0.15/GB/mo. A custom domain and its TLS cert are free (shared IPv4 is
included; first 10 certs per org are $0).

New Fly accounts have **no free tier** — this is pay-as-you-go.

**Hosting is the small number.** Your LLM and TTS API spend — podcast generation especially —
will dominate the bill. Open Notebook itself runs no models; it calls your providers.

## Deploy

Generate secrets first and keep them handy (don't commit them):
```bash
SURREALPW=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
ENCKEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
APPPW=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
```

`ENCKEY` encrypts the AI provider API keys you'll store in the database. **Save it somewhere
durable.** If you lose or change it, every stored credential becomes unreadable.

### 1. Database (private)
```bash
fly apps create open-notebook-db
# Allocate the private flycast address the app will dial:
fly ips allocate-v6 --private --app open-notebook-db
fly volumes create surreal_data --app open-notebook-db --region lax --size 1
fly secrets set --app open-notebook-db SURREAL_USER=notebook SURREAL_PASS="$SURREALPW"
fly deploy --config db/fly.toml
fly logs --app open-notebook-db   # watch for: "Started web server on [::]:8000"
```

Note the server reads `SURREAL_PASS`, while the app (next step) reads `SURREAL_PASSWORD`.
Different names, same value — this is upstream's naming, not a typo here.

### 2. App (public)
```bash
fly apps create open-notebook-af
fly volumes create notebook_data --app open-notebook-af --region lax --size 3
fly secrets set --app open-notebook-af \
  OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$ENCKEY" \
  OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD="$APPPW" \
  SURREAL_USER=notebook \
  SURREAL_PASSWORD="$SURREALPW"
fly deploy --config app/fly.toml
fly logs --app open-notebook-af
```

Watch for `Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:5055` and `Next.js ready on http://0.0.0.0:8502`,
with no repeating SurrealDB connection retries.

### 3. First login
Open `https://open-notebook-af.fly.dev`, enter `$APPPW`, then:
**Settings → API Keys → Add Credential** for your provider → **Test Connection** →
**Discover & Register Models**. Provider keys live in the database (encrypted with
`OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), not in `fly secrets`.

## Verify
1. `fly status` on both apps — db `started`; the app may show `suspended` until you hit it.
2. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $APPPW" https://open-notebook-af.fly.dev/api/config` → JSON.
   Without the header you should get `{"detail":"Missing authorization header"}` — that's the
   password gate working, not a bug.
3. Browser console (F12) should log
   `✅ [Config] Runtime API URL from server: https://open-notebook-af.fly.dev`.
   If it shows `:5055`, `API_URL` didn't take.
4. Create a notebook, add a URL as a source, wait for the worker to finish, reload → it persists.
5. Upload a ~20MB PDF → no 413.
6. `fly machine stop --app open-notebook-af <id>`, then load the URL again → it resumes and the
   data is still there. Confirms the volume and the auto-suspend path.
7. `fly ssh console --app open-notebook-db` → `ls -la /mydata/mydatabase.db` is non-empty.

## Ongoing
```bash
fly logs --app <app>                 # tail logs
fly status --app <app>               # machine status
fly ssh console --app <app>          # shell in
fly deploy --config <dir>/fly.toml   # redeploy after image/config change
```
Images are pinned to `:v1-latest` / `:v2`; `fly deploy` re-pulls. Pin to a digest if you want
reproducibility.

## Notes / gotchas

- **`.flycast`, not `.internal`, and `--bind '[::]:8000'`.** Fly's private network is IPv6.
  SurrealDB binds `127.0.0.1:8000` by default and even `0.0.0.0` is IPv4-only, so the default
  is unreachable from the other app. `db/fly.toml` does both: binds IPv6 *and* goes through
  flycast. The `fly ips allocate-v6 --private` step is required or `.flycast` won't resolve.

- **Auto-suspend tears down background jobs.** Fly suspends the machine when the proxy sees no
  active connections. A podcast or embedding job running with no browser tab open dies with it.
  `suspend` only shortens resume time (~1-3s vs a full boot) — it is not a fix for this.

  Either switch to the always-on values in `app/fly.toml` permanently, or pin the machine just
  for the long job and revert after:
  ```bash
  fly scale count 1 --app open-notebook-af   # and set min_machines_running = 1 in app/fly.toml
  ```

- **The database is always-on by design.** Auto-stopping it races the app's startup: the API
  opens its websocket immediately on boot and a cold-starting DB can lose that race. $3.32/mo
  buys you out of debugging intermittent boot failures.

- **`OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENCRYPTION_KEY` must never change** once you've saved a provider credential.
  Rotating it makes all stored keys unreadable, with no recovery path.

- **`OPEN_NOTEBOOK_PASSWORD` is the only authentication**, and it is not optional. It's a single
  shared password — no accounts, no login provider, nothing to administer. Leave it unset and
  anyone who reaches the URL gets full read/write access to your notebooks and can spend your
  provider API keys. Using the default `.fly.dev` hostname doesn't help: it's a public hostname
  with a public IP and app names are globally unique and enumerable.

- **Optional heavy extras.** `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENABLE_DOCLING` (local PDF/OCR via a large ML stack)
  and `OPEN_NOTEBOOK_ENABLE_CRAWL4AI` (bundles Chromium) are off. Each installs itself on first
  boot into `/app/data`, needs 4gb+ RAM, and pushes the machine to $22+/mo. Prefer the hosted
  equivalents — `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `JINA_API_KEY`, or a remote `CRAWL4AI_API_URL`.

- **One machine only.** A volume-attached app can't scale past a single machine, and deploys
  are not zero-downtime — Fly stops the old machine before starting the new one.

- **If the frontend can't reach the API**, try adding `API_HOST = '::'` to `app/fly.toml`
  `[env]`. Upstream offers it for IPv6 dual-stack environments. It's left out here because the
  API is only ever reached from `localhost` inside the container.

- **Custom domain** (optional, free): `fly certs add notebook.example.com`, add the DNS records
  Fly prints, then update `API_URL` and `CORS_ORIGINS` in `app/fly.toml` and redeploy.
